newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain king to make rare address after ETA killing.
newsitem.headline: Spain king to make rare address after ETA killing.

text.p: Spain's King Juan Carlos will make a rare address to the nation on Monday night in response to the brutal killing of a young politician by ETA Basque guerrillas, a palace spokesman said.

The king will speak to the nation on state television and radio at 7.45 p.m. (1745 GMT), 15 minutes before a huge demonstration led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar is scheduled to begin in central Madrid.

The king, who usually tries to stay clear of politics, sent his son Crown Prince Felipe to the funeral of town councillor Miguel Angel Blanco in the Basque town of Ermua on Monday. Aznar also attended the funeral.
"I came to express the pain of the royal family and its condemnation of this terrorist act," the prince said at the burial ceremony in Ermua's cemetery.

"I want to take advantage of the occasion to express the support of the royal family for the Basque people in this calm, civil and peaceful struggle against ETA terrorism and its accomplices," he said.

The king has rarely addressed the nation apart from his regular speech at Christmas. In 1981, the king made a speech after military officers stormed Parliament and held legislators hostage in an attempted coup.
"It's not normal that the king makes an address like this, but he thinks it is opportune at this time," the palace spokesman said.
Officials believe Monday's demonstration in Madrid could reach the same proportions as the street protest after the coup attempt, which was the largest in Spanish history.

Blanco, 29, was killed after ETA rebels kidnapped him and demanded the government move about 500 ETA inmates to the Basque region before 4 p.m on Saturday. He was found bound and bloodied with two gunshot wounds in his head shortly after the deadline on Saturday and died some 12 hours later.
His killing has sparked an angry public outcry against the rebel group ETA, with more than a million Spaniards taking to the streets in protest over the weekend.
